title: Derived internal Hom into a K-injective and its derived global sections
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site that is small in the sense of [def-weil-size-convention] and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use the category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], its unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], Hom complexes $\mathcal Hom^\bullet$ [def-pur-hom-complex], and K-flat and K-injective complexes [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The derived tensor product $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}N$ is represented by $\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal P^\bullet\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal N^\bullet)$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] for a K-flat complex $\mathcal P^\bullet$ representing $K$ and any complex $\mathcal N^\bullet$ representing $N$. Fix $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and let $H_K:D(\mathcal O)\to D(\mathcal O)$ be any right adjoint of $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O}-$ . Let $\mathcal A^\bullet$ be any complex of $\mathcal O$-modules representing $K$, and let $\mathcal J^\bullet$ be a K-injective complex representing $M\in D(\mathcal O)$. Then:

1. There is an isomorphism $H_K(M)\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet)$ in $D(\mathcal O)$, natural with respect to morphisms of K-injective complexes $\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$.
2. The derived global sections $R\Gamma(\mathcal C,H_K(M))$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology] are represented, in the derived category of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], by the complex of global morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet)=\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet))$, whose degree-$n$ term is $\prod_{p\in\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal A^p,\mathcal J^{p+n})$, naturally with respect to morphisms of complexes $\mathcal A'^\bullet\to\mathcal A^\bullet$ and of K-injective complexes $\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$. In particular $H^n R\Gamma(\mathcal C,H_K(M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K,M[n])$ for every integer $n$.

No boundedness of $K$ or $M$ and no flatness of $\mathcal A^\bullet$ is assumed.

source.place: Section 'Internal hom in the derived category' (Tag 08J7, label section-internal-hom): the construction $R\mathcal Hom(L,M)=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal L^\bullet,\mathcal I^\bullet)$ with equation-internal-hom and Yoneda; Lemma 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U); Lemma 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom); Lemma 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective).

proof.text: Choose a K-flat resolution $r:\mathcal P^\bullet\to\mathcal A^\bullet$ by [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Put $B_{\mathcal A}=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal A^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet)$ and $C=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal P^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet)$. By [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined], applied to $r$ and the identity of the K-injective $\mathcal J^\bullet$, precomposition gives a quasi-isomorphism $r^*:B_{\mathcal A}\to C$. By [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], $C$ is K-injective. The definition [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] therefore represents its functor $R\mathcal Hom(K,M)$ by either $B_{\mathcal A}$ or $C$, with the canonical comparison just described, functorial in chain maps of the representatives. The hypotheses here are precisely a small ringed site, a K-flat source resolution, and a K-injective target; $\mathcal A^\bullet$ itself need not be flat.

For $N\in D(\mathcal O)$ represented by any complex $\mathcal B^\bullet$, compute
$$\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(N,QC)&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\mathcal B^\bullet,C)\\&\cong H^0\Gamma\bigl(\mathcal C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal B^\bullet,C)\bigr)\\&\cong H^0\Gamma\bigl(\mathcal C,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal B^\bullet\otimes\mathcal P^\bullet),\mathcal J^\bullet)\bigr)\\&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal O)}(\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal B^\bullet\otimes\mathcal P^\bullet),\mathcal J^\bullet)\\&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(Q\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal B^\bullet\otimes\mathcal P^\bullet),M).\end{aligned}$$
The first and last bijections are [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived], since $C$ and $\mathcal J^\bullet$ are K-injective. The second and fourth are [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-homotopy]; the middle one is [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total], whose statement is for arbitrary ringed sites, despite its prefix. All are natural in $\mathcal B^\bullet$ and in maps of K-injective targets. To match the tensor order in the item, exchange the summand $\mathcal B^q\otimes\mathcal P^p$ with $\mathcal P^p\otimes\mathcal B^q$ using $b\otimes x\mapsto(-1)^{pq}x\otimes b$. With the differential in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], the two differential components commute with this exchange because $(p+1)q=pq+q$ and $p(q+1)+p\equiv pq\pmod2$. Exchanging twice is the identity. Thus $Q\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal B^\bullet\otimes\mathcal P^\bullet)\cong K\otimes^{\mathbf L}N$ by the tensor convention in the statement. This proves that $R\mathcal Hom(K,-)$ is a right adjoint to $K\otimes^{\mathbf L}-$, by the same representative calculation as Stacks 08J9; maps out of arbitrary derived objects are covered because localization inverts quasi-isomorphisms and the displayed bijections are natural on representatives.

proof.text: Compose the adjunction bijection for the given $H_K$ with that of step 2 to obtain a bijection $\theta_N:\operatorname{Hom}(N,H_K(M))\to\operatorname{Hom}(N,R\mathcal Hom(K,M))$ natural in $N$ and $M$. This gives an isomorphism without any extra hypothesis: put $f=\theta_{H_K(M)}(1)$ and $g=\theta^{-1}_{R\mathcal Hom(K,M)}(1)$. Naturality in $N$ says $\theta_N(a)=f\circ a$ and $\theta_N^{-1}(b)=g\circ b$; the two inverse-bijection identities give $gf=1$ and $fg=1$. Naturality in $M$ implies that $f$ commutes with maps $\mathcal J^\bullet\to\mathcal J'^\bullet$. Composing $f$ with the representative identification of step 1 gives clause (1). This is the explicit Yoneda uniqueness argument of Section 08J7. For varying first argument the same construction uses precomposition in $R\mathcal Hom$; equivalently it is the map induced between the right adjoints by the tensor morphism, so the identification also respects chain maps $\mathcal A'^\bullet\to\mathcal A^\bullet$.

source.place: Section 08J7 (section-internal-hom), equation-internal-hom and the following Yoneda uniqueness sentence

proof.text:
We need ordinary global sections of $B_{\mathcal A}$ to compute its derived sections, even though $B_{\mathcal A}$ need not be K-injective. First compute ordinary global Hom cohomology in every degree. For any complex $\mathcal T^\bullet$ and integer $n$, [def-pur-hom-complex] gives the chain isomorphism $\Gamma\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal T,\mathcal J)[n]\cong\Gamma\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal T,\mathcal J[n])$ by identity on each component indexed by $p$ (the differentials on both sides are $(-1)^n d_{\mathcal J}f-(-1)^a f d_{\mathcal T}$ in degree $a$). Apply [lem-pur-hom-complex-global-homotopy] in degree zero to $\mathcal T$ and $\mathcal J[n]$. The complex $\mathcal J[n]$ is K-injective directly from [def-pur-kinjective-complex]: a map from acyclic $V$ to $\mathcal J[n]$ is a shifted map from the acyclic $V[-n]$ to $\mathcal J$, so its null homotopy shifts back. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] gives, naturally in both variables,
$$H^n\Gamma\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal T,\mathcal J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(Q\mathcal T,M[n]).$$
Take $\mathcal T=\mathcal A$ and $\mathcal T=\mathcal P$. The map on these groups induced by $\Gamma(r^*)$ is precomposition with $Qr$, which is invertible because $r$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus $\Gamma(r^*):\Gamma B_{\mathcal A}\to\Gamma C$ is a quasi-isomorphism of abelian-group complexes. This uses no exactness assumption on $\Gamma$ or on infinite products.

source.place: Equation 0A8Z (equation-global-cohomology-hom-complex); Tag 0A94 (lemma-RHom-into-K-injective), global calculation; derived.tex Tags 070H and 070I

proof.text:
Use the unbounded K-injective definition of $R\Gamma$ in [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], with the functorial K-injective resolutions in [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The resolution maps give a natural comparison $\delta_E:Q_{\operatorname{Ab}}\Gamma E\to R\Gamma(QE)$ for every sheaf complex $E$. When $E$ is K-injective, its resolution map is a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives and hence a homotopy equivalence by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]; applying $\Gamma$ preserves its inverse and homotopy equations. Thus $\delta_C$ is an isomorphism. In the naturality square for $r^*:B_{\mathcal A}\to C$, the upper horizontal arrow $Q_{\operatorname{Ab}}\Gamma(r^*)$ is invertible by step 4, and the lower horizontal arrow $R\Gamma(Qr^*)$ is invertible by step 1. Consequently
$$\delta_{B_{\mathcal A}}=(R\Gamma(Qr^*))^{-1}\,\delta_C\,Q_{\operatorname{Ab}}\Gamma(r^*)$$
is invertible. Together with clause (1), this proves the asserted representation of $R\Gamma(\mathcal C,H_K(M))$ by $\Gamma B_{\mathcal A}$. The comparison $\delta$ is natural before the auxiliary choice of $\mathcal P$, so this identification is natural for all chain maps $\mathcal A'\to\mathcal A$ and all maps of K-injectives $\mathcal J\to\mathcal J'$. No natural choice of K-flat resolution is needed for that conclusion.

source.place: Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), proof using 0A96 and 0A94; Section 07A5 (section-unbounded); functorial resolutions via injectives.tex Tag 079P

proof.text: Finally, [def-pur-hom-complex] computes the degree-$n$ term of $\Gamma B_{\mathcal A}$ by taking sections of $\prod_p\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal A^p,\mathcal J^{p+n})$. Global sections commute with these products: a morphism $\mathcal O\to\prod_p F_p$ is exactly a family of morphisms $\mathcal O\to F_p$. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom], global sections of each factor are $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(\mathcal A^p,\mathcal J^{p+n})$. Its differential is $d_{\mathcal J}f-(-1)^n f d_{\mathcal A}$, so the resulting complex is exactly the stated global morphism complex, not just a termwise identification. Pre- and postcomposition are the maps of this complex by the functoriality in [def-pur-hom-complex]. Combining step 5 with the degree-$n$ calculation of step 4 for $\mathcal T=\mathcal A$ gives $H^nR\Gamma(\mathcal C,H_K(M))\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O)}(K,M[n])$ for all integers $n$, proving the final assertion of clause (2).
